title: Snowpeak: render 3D at 4x/8x, then pixelate + shipped fix chain (S4_hd2, S4_hd)
question: Is pixel art better if we render the same model/pose/camera at high resolution, downscale with k-centroid, RD pixel-fixer, majority vote or area average, and then run the fix pass, instead of using the native sprite-resolution pass?
method: The hi-res tracer fires the same rays as render_pixels(ss=k) and keeps a buffer per sample (k=4,8): depth, normal, lambert, material, group, band, smooth and flat RGB. An edge pass marks depth breaks and normal creases. Each method resolves to a 48x64 PixelFrame. A runtime swap of frames.render_pixels then runs the whole shipped fix chain on each one (face cels, pixelrules, sel-out outline, ring trim, bow shine, orphans, temporal_hold). Coverage: S4_hd2 idle/walk/run x 8 dirs x 8 frames; S4_hd idle/walk (run S/SE/E). Scripts in exp/2026-10-28_snowpeak_hires/scripts.
result: Native re-render = shipped (0 px diff). Orphans are 0 for every method and height deltas are unchanged. S4_hd2 idle, native vs best hi-res (KC, k=8): jaggies 0.55 vs 0.92 per frame, coat islands 0.06 vs 0.33 per frame, ABA boil 3.38 vs 2.98. Walk: jaggies 1.00 vs 1.53, ABA 53.2 vs 53.9. The pixel-fixer is worst (walk ABA 58.4; idle diff vs native 21%). k=4 and k=8 give near-identical results.
verdict: Rejected. Argon: N 6, KC 6 (same), VM 5.5, KCE 4.5, PF 3.5. Opus: N 6, KC 6 (same), VM 5, KCE 5, PF 3. Both critics: high-res fixes none of the six known problems (coat slab, mitten islands, stub legs, blob hands, small S bow, fringe ridges). These come from the model and design, not from sampling. Normal-buffer interior lines come out broken dashes that boil.
